findings.text: the allowance aggregate counts a row whose seven-day clock was never observed as reproduced, because pace_replay.py:211-212 returns None for an unobserved clock and _same_value(None, None) then matches the row's null allowance: replaying the unpaced live pointer for run r-20260926T210659299521 (clocks.seven_day.state unknown, allowance null) prints "allowances: 1/1 reproduced (ok)" and ok true, so a week in which nothing was measured reports a full score and a tuning reader cannot tell it from a validated one.

the hold check falls back to the row's stored held flag when the threshold and utilisation evidence is absent, which is the value _recorded_hold_decision reads on the other side of the comparison, so a hold carrying a bare verdict compares equal to itself and is counted reproduced - demonstrated by a row with hold {"backend": "codex", "held": true} reporting "holds: 1/1 reproduced (ok)", while the same row with evidence present (held false against 95.0% >= 92.0%) is correctly reported as a mismatch, which is the positive control the fallback path lacks.

an unidentified lane is classified metered rather than unknown, so a row carrying no lane kind, no local flag and no backend or lane name is counted into the metered column of the split the plan asks to be reproducible, asserting a lane choice the record never made.
